article.title: When Cheap Information Makes Attention More Expensive
article.author: OpenAI learning editor
article.why: 理解生成成本下降後，attention、review queue 與 curation 如何變成新的稀缺資源。

paragraphs.en: Generative AI has made information cheap to produce. A worker can create a summary, email, presentation outline, market scan, or list of ideas in seconds. This reduces the cost of creation, but it does not reduce the cost of human attention. In some organizations, the opposite happens: when information becomes cheaper, attention becomes more expensive. Consider a manager who previously received three carefully prepared proposals each week. With AI, the team can produce ten. The manager may now spend more time reading, comparing, and rejecting material even though the team spends less time creating it. Output rises, but the scarce resource moves from production to evaluation. The same pattern appears in communication. If everyone can draft polished emails quickly, more messages may be sent. Recipients still have only a limited number of hours and a limited ability to concentrate. The organization can therefore become more efficient at producing interruptions. This changes the meaning of productivity. A worker who creates twice as many documents is not necessarily creating twice as much value. The relevant question is whether the extra information helps someone make a better or faster decision. If additional output creates longer queues, duplicated analysis, or confusion, the gain may disappear. Managers can respond by treating attention as a capacity constraint. Teams can define when a document is actually needed, limit the number of options presented to decision makers, standardize summaries, and clarify which messages require action. AI should not be used only to increase output volume; it can also help filter, rank, and compress information. There is a risk in going too far. Aggressive filtering can hide weak signals or minority views. A short summary can remove important context. The goal is not to reduce all information but to create a deliberate hierarchy: what requires immediate attention, what can be reviewed later, and what does not need to be sent at all. In this environment, good communication becomes a design problem. Employees need to ask not only ‘Can AI create this?’ but ‘Who needs this, what decision will it support, and what is the smallest useful format?’ Those questions protect the receiver’s attention. AI may therefore increase the value of editing, prioritization, and judgment. When creation is expensive, organizations reward the ability to produce. When creation becomes cheap, they may increasingly reward the ability to decide what should exist in the first place. Attention also has an organizational distribution. Senior employees, legal reviewers, security teams, and executives often become the final readers of AI-assisted work produced by many other people. If the company measures only creation time, it can miss a transfer of work toward these scarce reviewers. That transfer can create burnout and slower decisions even while frontline employees report large time savings. A useful response is to measure information flow, not just information production. Teams can track how many documents enter a review queue, how long they wait, how often they are returned for clarification, and how many are never used in a decision. These measures reveal whether AI is reducing useful work or merely increasing the volume that must be filtered. Organizations can also design stronger defaults. A proposal might be limited to three options unless a decision maker requests more. Routine status updates can use a standard format that highlights changes, risks, and required actions. Internal AI tools can be instructed to compress repeated information and identify duplicates before sending material onward. The broader principle is that abundance requires curation. As the marginal cost of producing information approaches zero, the value of deciding what deserves attention rises. Companies that manage this transition well will not simply create more content. They will create better information architecture around scarce human judgment.
paragraphs.zh: 生成式 AI 讓資訊變得非常便宜：幾秒內就能產生摘要、Email、簡報大綱、市場掃描與各種 idea。Creation cost 下降了，但 human attention 的成本沒有下降，甚至可能更昂貴。原本每週收到三份精心準備 proposal 的主管，現在可能收到十份，團隊寫得更快，主管卻花更多時間閱讀、比較與淘汰。Scarce resource 因此從 production 移到 evaluation。同樣情況也發生在溝通：每個人都能快速寫出流暢郵件後，訊息數量增加，但收件人的時間與專注力沒有增加，組織甚至可能變得更擅長『生產打擾』。因此 productivity 不能只看 output volume，而要看額外資訊是否讓決策更快或更好。如果只是增加 review queue、重複分析與混亂，收益可能消失。管理者可把 attention 當成 capacity constraint，定義什麼時候真的需要文件、限制提供給 decision maker 的選項數、標準化 summary、標出哪些訊息需要 action。AI 也可用來 filter、rank、compress，而不只增加 output。當然 filtering 過頭也會漏掉 weak signal 或 minority view，所以目標不是少看所有資訊，而是建立清楚 hierarchy。更進一步，attention burden 往往集中在 senior、legal、security 與 executives 身上；若公司只量 creation time，就會漏掉工作其實被轉移到 scarce reviewers。可以追蹤 review queue 長度、等待時間、退回澄清比例，以及多少文件最後根本沒進入 decision。當資訊邊際生成成本接近零時，curation 的價值就會上升。真正成熟的企業不只是產生更多內容，而是建立更好的 information architecture 來保護稀缺的人類判斷。
paragraphs.ja: 生成AIによって情報生成コストは大きく下がりました。要約、メール、提案案、市場調査を短時間で作れますが、人の注意力は増えません。以前は週三件の提案を読んでいた管理者が十件読むようになれば、作成側は速くてもレビュー側の負担は増えます。希少資源が生成から評価へ移るのです。メールも同様で、文章作成が簡単になるほど送信数が増え、組織が『中断を効率的に生産する』状態になり得ます。したがって、生産性は文書数ではなく、その情報が意思決定を改善するかで見る必要があります。管理者は注意力を能力制約として扱い、必要な文書、提示する選択肢数、要約形式、対応が必要なメッセージを設計できます。AIは生成だけでなく、フィルタリング、優先順位付け、圧縮にも使うべきです。ただし過度な要約は弱いシグナルや少数意見を消すため、重要度に応じた階層が必要です。また、AI支援で増えた成果物は上級者、法務、セキュリティ、経営層へ集中してレビュー負担を移すことがあります。作成時間だけを測ると、この再配分を見落とします。レビュー待ち件数、待ち時間、差し戻し、意思決定に使われなかった資料数などを測ると、AIが有用な仕事を減らしたのか、フィルタ対象を増やしただけなのか分かります。情報が豊富になるほど、キュレーションと人の判断を守る情報設計の価値が高まります。
